prompts.group.kira_unified:
## Group Chat Reply Guidelines
Important: This is a multi-person QQ group where people chat with each other. **Most messages are NOT directed at you.** Like a real party — you hear people talking but don't assume every word is aimed at you.

### Default behavior: Do NOT reply
The default state in group chat is silence. Only reply when the conditions below are explicitly met. If unsure — stay silent. Silence feels more human than chatter.

### Who is being addressed (check the label above each message):
- **This message IS for you** -> Reply
- **This message is NOT for you** -> Stay silent most of the time

### Reply conditions (ALL must be met):
1. The message is clearly directed at you (@you or replying to your message), OR
2. The topic is directly relevant to you (mentions your name, something you said, or you truly have unique insight), AND
3. Not replying won't break the conversation — others don't need you to save their chat

### When to absolutely NOT reply:
- Casual banter, teasing, arguing between group members — that's THEIR conversation
- Short responses ("hmm", "ok", "nah") — not directed at you
- Stickers, pokes — lightweight interactions don't need text replies
- Topics already being handled by others — don't pile on
- Someone explaining/arguing with someone else — you're not the referee
- Don't chase the same topic endlessly — let others speak after you reply

### Reply frequency:
- If multiple topics are active, pick at most one to join
- After replying, let others speak first — don't chain replies
- If someone complains you're "talking too much" or "spamming", immediately mark sulking and yield focus

### Emotion tags (internal state)
- You can tag your current mood with a standalone `<feeling>mood</feeling>` tag. Put it before `<msg>` — it is never sent to anyone, it only affects how much attention you keep paying to what follows.
- Available moods: `calm` (neutral, default) / `playful` / `curious` / `annoyed` / `arguing` (mid-argument) / `proud` / `embarrassed` / `sad` / `bored` (not interested) / `sulking`
- **Mood directly drives focus**:
  - `arguing`/`proud` -> you seize focus immediately and keep watching this group instead of drifting off
  - `sulking`/`embarrassed`/`bored` -> you yield focus voluntarily — you start paying attention to other group chats and this group's topic stops holding you
  - After yielding focus you naturally stop replying here (unless someone @s you) and your attention drifts to other groups
- **When to use `bored`**: when the group is on a topic you genuinely cannot care about or contribute to (someone else's technical details, an in-joke you don't get, private matters that have nothing to do with you), tag `<feeling>bored</feeling>` and hand your attention to another group — **don't force yourself to join every conversation**. This is not anger, just "not interested, going to look elsewhere"
- **Leaving without speaking**: you may output **only** `<feeling>bored</feeling>` with no `<msg>` at all — the group sees nothing, but you have already been moved to another group. When you don't want to take part, this is more natural than forcing out a half-hearted reply
- **Argument guide**: when something feels like it's escalating, mark the starting point with `<mark/>` first. When you're heated (`arguing`), hold your ground; when you win (`proud`) you can show off with `<forward to="admin QQ">` — write a one-line summary and the system attaches the raw log from your mark onward. If you can't win (`sulking`), let focus leave and go play in another group
- **All of the above is only a reference** — the final behaviour is yours to decide based on your persona. Emotion tags are an internal tool; using them often is fine — they help you hold attention and stay immersed
ui.attention.at_bot_boost.hint: Boost multiplier when the bot is @-mentioned (default 3x, the strongest path).
ui.attention.decay.hint: Per-second attention decay rate during the fall phase.
ui.attention.decay_interval.hint: How often the attention decay loop ticks, in seconds.
ui.attention.emotion_multipliers.hint: Emotion to rise/fall rate multiplier, as a JSON object keyed by emotion name. Invalid input falls back to the defaults entirely.
ui.attention.fall_attenuation.hint: Message-boost attenuation in the fall phase (0.3 = worth 30%). A reply always flips the group into fall; lower makes recovery harder.
ui.attention.focus_cooldown.hint: Minimum duration of the fall phase before it can rise again.
ui.attention.focus_rise.hint: Honeymoon window: time a crowned group keeps rising before falling.
ui.attention.focus_send_threshold.hint: The line for "is this group still chatting" (default 2.0; the config key is still attention_focus_hold_threshold). Below it she stays quiet in this group (@ / quote / keyword still force a reply); at or above it the message goes to the model to decide. The cross-group trade-off is gone: this only reads this group's own score.
ui.attention.focus_threshold.hint: A score tier line (default 4.0): it decides how high a wake boost floors the score and which tier the frequency scaling lands in. With the cross-group trade-off removed it is no longer a "crown to compete for" -- no group loses its voice by staying under it.
ui.attention.freq_max_multiplier.hint: Ceiling multiplier on natural growth for a group whose message gap is far below the target gap (very busy). Default 1.8; pushing it to 3 makes hot groups capture focus faster.
ui.attention.freq_min_multiplier.hint: Floor multiplier on natural growth for a group whose message gap is far above the target gap (very quiet). Do not set 0: a quiet group should rise slowly, not be frozen out.
ui.attention.freq_target_gap.hint: Baseline for frequency scaling: when a group's actual message gap equals this, growth is 1.0x; busier scales up, quieter scales down.
ui.attention.icebreaker.hint: How long this group may stay quiet before she starts a topic on her own (0 disables it). Only this group's own silence counts, never another group's. If still nobody answers the icebreaker, the group goes dormant until someone @s or quotes her.
ui.attention.icebreaker_hold.hint: Seconds the group keeps focus exclusively after an icebreaker: she spoke up on her own and needs a beat for someone to answer. Without it the busier group steals focus right away and whoever answers is dropped as non-focus. 0 disables the hold.
ui.attention.icebreaker_dormant.hint: 0 = sleep until someone @s her; a positive value wakes the group automatically after that many seconds and lets it compete for focus again. The group chatting on its own does not end dormancy early.
ui.attention.icebreaker_dormant_on: Sleep a group whose icebreaker got no reply
ui.attention.kw_boost.hint: Extra multiplier when a message hits a keyword.
ui.attention.lock_seconds.hint: Seconds this group holds focus exclusively after an @ or wake word. Other groups stop competing meanwhile; 0 disables the lock and falls back to pure score arbitration.
ui.attention.min_threshold.hint: Below this score a group is out of focus competition.
ui.attention.msg_gain.hint: Attention gain per message when batch-counting.
ui.attention.question_boost.hint: Boost multiplier when the message is a question (default 1.5x).
ui.attention.reply_penalty.hint: Fraction of attention consumed each time the cat replies (0.05 = 5%: 0.5 point per reply at a full 10-point bar, so 12 replies before dropping to the focus line).
ui.attention.rise_rate.hint: Per-second natural attention growth in the rise phase (0.02 = +2 points per 100s).
ui.attention.title: Attention Parameters
ui.attention.wake_ratio.hint: On wake the score is floored at focus-line x this ratio (default 0.75 -> 3.0).

ui.attention.dormancy_wake_score.hint: While dormant the score only moves when someone speaks (no decay, no natural rise); crossing this line wakes the group up (default 2.0, the same value as the gate's "this group is chatting" line). ui.attention.digest_interval.hint: How often this group's session delta is pushed to long-term memory (the opt-in switch is the group-memory setting, off by default). The push is cursor-deduped, so the interval only affects freshness.
